text:
router-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in router-prod-usw2. Start=2026-03-15T15:03:10Z. Affected surfaces: streaming /v1/generate and a subset of short-chat routes. p95 ~420ms (SLO 200ms), p99 ~2300ms (SLO 600ms). Error rate normal. Triggering paging and channel notification.

pagerduty: paging miguel (oncall).

miguel (oncall): acked, jumping in. Any deploys around 15:00?

anne (infra): no infra deploys at 14:50-15:10. We saw a routing-policy rollout at 14:58 (policy-id: rp-2026-03-15-19). It adjusted shard weights for region-aware balancing.

priyanka (product): seeing customer reports of stalls in streaming, some sessions long-pause then resume. Not universal. Link to customer impact dashboard: https://internal/dashboards/routing/p99-spike (repro link).

chen (eng-runtime): pulling router logs. Early signs: one hash partition (shard 7a4) has sustained connection skew; backend pool for that shard is saturated. KV cache hit rate unchanged. Looks like weight skew sent ~60% of traffic to a small subset of backends.

miguel (oncall): can we confirm whether this is a routing-policy misassignment vs backend health?

chen (eng-runtime): health checks OK. CPU/GPU on backends showing high accept queue and elevated tail latency. Backend logs show a few streaming stall stacks:

```
stream-stall: conn_id=0x7fa4fd, last-progress=12s
stack: wait_for_kv_cache -> send_chunk -> flush -> stalled on network-write
```

No OOMs. No pod restarts.

anne (infra): checked LB state: routing-policy rollout updated weights via the control plane but one seed list for zone-west2 was accidentally duplicated due to a merge bug; duplication caused hash distribution to collapse to fewer backends. Here is the weight snapshot showing skew:

```
shard 7a4: total weight 0.58
  backend-a (zone-west2-1): 0.29
  backend-b (zone-west2-2): 0.20
  backend-c (zone-west2-3): 0.09
others: spread across >30 backends but not matching consistent hash buckets
```

anne (infra): root cause candidate: routing-policy generator returned duplicate seed entries for the same zone (bug rp-gen#142). That made the consistent-hash ring map many keys to the same few backends.

miguel (oncall): mitigation options?

chen (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: 1) rollback the policy to previous version (rp-2026-03-15-18) 2) apply emergency weight-cap (cap per-backend <= 0.12) 3) divert traffic for streaming routes to fallback pool (less efficient) 4) add temporary backends to the hot pool. Rollback is fastest.

anne (infra): rolling policy rollback now. Command: `infractl routing-policy rollback --id rp-2026-03-15-18 --region usw2` (running).

sre-bot: rollout-rollback started by anne at 15:06:12 UTC.

miguel (oncall): monitoring metrics in 30s. Also preparing a livepage with customer-facing note if p99 stays >1s for 10m.

(prior to rollback completing) priyanka (product): which customers are impacted most? I see a cluster of heavy-usage tenants on long-context streaming sessions. Top impacted tenant ids: tenant-53, tenant-87, tenant-echo (count-based filter). Estimated impacted requests ~0.9% of total (about 5k reqs/min).

chen (eng-runtime): rollback confirmed 15:07:03 UTC. Routing weights are reverting. Started rebalancing; backend accept queues dropping.

sre-bot: telemetry: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 210ms over next 40s; p99 trending down from 2.3s -> 650ms.

miguel (oncall): good. keep watching for 10m. Any lessons about rollout gating?

anne (infra): we should add a preflight check to detect duplicate seeds and an integration test in rp-gen pipeline. Also add a safety cap in the router that prevents a single backend exceeding 0.2 of shard weight. Filing infra ticket INFRA-2026-332.

priyanka (product): coordinating comms. Drafting a short customer advisory for affected tenants: apology + summary + mitigation + follow-up postmortem. Will post to status.redwood if p99 stays high.

chen (eng-runtime): follow-up ops: 1) run a conformance check across all regions for rp-gen duplication 2) add a canary rollout for routing-policy to 5% traffic. 3) add telemetry alert for per-backend weight >0.25.

miguel (oncall): handing off to anne for infra-led remediation and postmortem. I'm back on-call watch but moving to monitoring. Assigned owner: anne -> lead for incident.

anne (infra): taking owner. I've captured timeline and assigned follow-ups: INFRA-2026-332 (seed duplication root cause, patch rp-gen), RUNBOOK-UPDATE-23 (safety cap), ONCALL-PLAY-ADD (canary for policy rollouts).

priyanka (product): noted. ETA for customer advisory draft: 30m. Postmortem owner request: priyanka to drive customer comms and chen to own technical RCA.

miguel (oncall): closing livepage if p99 stable <700ms for 15m and no new regressions.

sre-bot: incident summary (automated):
- start: 2026-03-15T15:03:10Z
- mitigation: routing-policy rollback at 15:07:03Z
- impact: p99 spike to ~2.3s; affected ~0.9% traffic; streaming stalls observed; error rate unchanged
- probable cause: routing-policy generator produced duplicated seed entries -> hash concentration on small backend set -> hot partition -> tail latency spikes
- next steps: patch rp-gen, add weight cap, add canary rollouts, update runbook

anne (infra): leaving notes in the incident channel and creating postmortem doc. Adding links: https://internal/infra/tickets/INFRA-2026-332 and https://internal/pm/incidents/1880123456.

miguel (oncall): ack. Good work. Stand down contingent on 15m stability. :thumbsup:

chen (eng-runtime): will follow up with trace samples and a minimal reproducer of seed-dup scenario.

priyanka (product): sending customer advisory in 25m.

sre-bot: incident closed to livepage watchers at 15:34:40Z (p99 stable). Postmortem assigned.

(End of thread)
